elements.element: Renewal must occur only by mutual written agreement, unless the agreement instead uses the permitted automatic-renewal structure.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause states that renewal may occur “only by mutual written agreement of the parties.”

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, each automatic renewal term must be twelve (12) months.
elements.evidence: Automatic renewal is demonstrably absent because renewal requires mutual written agreement. The clause also independently limits renewal periods to twelve months.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, Customer must be permitted to opt out on thirty (30) days’ notice.
elements.evidence: Automatic renewal is demonstrably absent, so the conditional opt-out requirement is not triggered.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, Vendor must provide a renewal reminder sixty (60) days before renewal.
elements.evidence: Automatic renewal is demonstrably absent, so the conditional reminder requirement is not triggered.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must be capped at the lesser of CPI and three percent (3%).
elements.evidence: The rendered clause caps any renewal fee increase at “the lesser of the increase in the Consumer Price Index over the preceding period and three percent (3%).”
The rendered clause requires mutual written agreement for renewal and therefore does not provide automatic renewal.

elements.element: Customer must be able to prevent automatic renewal through a non-renewal notice window requiring no more than sixty (60) days’ advance notice.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no automatic-renewal mechanism or corresponding non-renewal notice right or window.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must not exceed five percent (5%).
elements.evidence: The lesser-of-CPI-and-3% cap necessarily limits any renewal fee increase to no more than 3%, which is within the 5% fallback ceiling.

result.reason: The operative language satisfies the mutual-written-agreement branch of the preferred position and includes the required CPI/3% cap. The automatic-renewal conditions are not triggered. It does not satisfy the fallback because renewal is not automatic and there is no non-renewal notice window. The revision preserves unrelated termination and payment provisions and aligns with the existing mutual-agreement language in Sections II and III. It is not strictly minimal because imposing twelve-month terms is unnecessary to satisfy the mutual-written-agreement branch. Drafting quality is reduced by redundancy across Sections I–III, the malformed phrase “mutual written of the parties,” and the lack of a more precise CPI definition.
